Definition: 3rd person plural present indicative of G1510; they are:--agree, are, be, dure, X is, were.
BiblicalUsage: This is the word they are, the third person plural of the verb to be, and in the Greek text it stands as a single form with a grave accent, not the acute accent Strong's lists. It occurs once, when Paul says the witnesses of the resurrection are the men who came up with Jesus from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now His witnesses to the people. One small form carries the whole testimony of the risen Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the witnesses are still speaking, because the men who saw Him risen could not keep quiet, and their word reaches me today.
